The man I had sent over the edge into death with these very hands was standing in front of me and laughing.
And what a size he had chosen for doing it. A giant reaching into the clouds.

Only, there was no warm bed waiting underneath it. No waking up and finding it had all been a dream.

en.html:
The metallic ring of my armor's voice warned me of danger.

Danger. Haan, that was the point I needed to remember.
I shoved all the questions into a corner of my head and forced it to attend to the present problem.

If THAT thing went down among human settlements, what chance did anyone have of coming through unharmed?
This was no Gulliver out of a fanciful travel book. The man was drunk on godhood. Expecting him to mind where the little people lived would be optimism beyond all reasonable limits.

And the shape had changed, but the thing inside was still the god. Still the source of the contamination waves spreading across the world.

One job for me. The same job as before.

ja.html:
劒冑の金打声が危険を告げる。

　危険――そう、これは危険！
　俺は異常事態への疑問を頭の隅に追いやり、思考の
切り替えを己に強要した。

　あんなものが人里へ降りて、無事に済む筈もない。
　空想旅行記の<ruby>巨人<rt>ガリバー</rt></ruby>とは違う。〝神〟の力に酔う風の
あの男に<ruby>小人<rt>・・</rt></ruby>の世界への配慮を期待するのは、希望的
観測が過ぎている。

　加えてあれは形こそ変われど〝神〟、全世界に蔓延
してゆく汚染波の源なのだ。
　
　俺のやるべき事は一つだった。

〝神〟は戦闘能力を飛躍的に増強した。
　間違いなく――如何なる所以ゆえんによってか長坂右京を
頭脳に得た一事で。

en.html:
No longer a monster throwing gravity about any which way.
All that immense power now had an experienced warrior directing it. And he had even remade the body into a dragoon—the shape he knew best how to handle. A demon-god.

Where there had been no tactics, now there was cunning.
Where power had gone everywhere wastefully, now it was being put exactly where it could do its work.

No doubt about either point. And comparing our strengths had become very simple.

In the beginning, the god had the entire advantage in power. I had the entire advantage in tactics.
Once Nagasaka became its brain, tactics came close to equal. Even then, it seemed he still had the disadvantage of operating that unfamiliar body.

置かれ、しかも彼が最も操りやすい<ruby>竜騎兵型<rt>かたち</rt></ruby>へと変貌
すらしている――<ruby>魔神<rt>サターン</rt></ruby>なのだ。

　皆無であった戦術構想は狡猾な進化を、
　粗雑であった力量使用は劇的な効率化を、
　
　遂げているとみて疑いない。
　戦力比較は今や単純化されている。

それでもまだ慣れぬ異形を操る不利は〝神〟側に存在
したと思われる。

Because now it was sword against sword.
The calculations that worked against a human being, against a trained warrior, would work here too.

Yes, the difference in weight and power was ridiculous.
But those were conditions of the fight. Not its result.

If the bodies were unequal, then I needed a technique that would overturn that inequality.

I looked at the demon-god's guard and read the swordsmanship it expressed.

...Same as before. This old soldier Nagasaka could rage and shout all he liked, but not one scrap of that temper came into his actual fighting.

Drunk on the Metal God's power, thinking me no better than a miserable insect—and still, his sword showed no intention of coming at me in some thoughtless rush.
One mind. One blade. Quietly waiting for the chance that would kill.

en.html:
I recognized it and named it to myself.
Not my school. Still, Rokuhara Shinkage and I kept meeting. Some people meet relatives this frequently. I meet people explaining, by demonstration, how they intend to cut me into pieces. A little knowledge accumulates.

The demon-god's guard was solid.
Look properly, though: one opening. Thin as a thread.

Haan. That was the trap.

Make your defense completely perfect and the enemy gets time to think. Thinking is dangerous. Some fellow who has no business being clever may suddenly become clever, and now your perfect defense is lying on the floor asking what happened. Why take this trouble? Leave him one little hole yourself.

There, bhai. See? An opportunity. Yours only. Attack here.

And the grateful fellow spends his strength, his skill, his precious moment—all inside the little dance you have prepared for him. He thinks he is taking the initiative. You are deciding even the direction in which his stupidity will travel.

Give the enemy room to live and act, and through that, bring him down. The Life-Giving Sword. Very generous. Life is being given strictly on the understanding that it will shortly be taken back.

With a god's power behind it, Nagasaka's method became stronger still. Suppose he misjudged a parry and my blade got through: that body could bear it. Mine, on the other hand, could be slaughtered by one graze of his returning sword.

He could afford a mistake. I could not afford the edge of a mistake passing nearby.

A formula for certain victory.

—And my answer was:

見て取って、俺は胸腑に呟いた。
　他流儀だが、六波羅新陰流とは奇妙に関わりを持つ
事が多く、多少の知識を持っている。

　魔神の剣形は如何にも堅牢なもの。
　だが詳細に目を凝らせば、糸筋程度の隙が見える。

　それこそが<ruby>陥穽<rt>わな</rt></ruby>。

　完璧に防御を固めれば、対敵は考えを巡らせたすえ、

　我が想定の範囲内で敵を踊らせ、力と技と機を無為
に費えさせるのだ。さすれば勝利はいとも容易い。
　
　――敵を<ruby>活<rt>い</rt></ruby>かして斃す、これぞ活人刀。

そして返す太刀は掠める程度で充分、敵を虐殺する。

　必勝の術式。
　
　
　――対するに、俺は、

en.html:
The demon-god seemed to smile with complete satisfaction.
He had probably understood my intention.

—Go along with his swordsmanship.

Take the bait he was offering.
Poison included. Eat the whole thing.

Take the initiative and attack exactly where he had deliberately left room for me.

Against his deep, elaborate principle, put one very crude and simple principle.

—Strike first. Kill first. Win before he does.

Setsunintou. The Life-Taking Sword.
Of course the demon-god sneered.

The basic method was the same as Magatsu, one of the electromagnetic draw forms.
Muramasa, the armor, produced a tremendous magnetic repulsion between sheath and blade. I, the wielder, guided that torrent into the drawing cut.
The method had not changed. Only the quantity.
The scale. The speed. The force.

If the ordinary sword could hold a hundred units of fighting power, Kotetsu, the nodachi, could hold ten thousand.

en.text:
At the very last moment, the demon-god finally made the right decision.
Threw away the Life-Giving Sword's principle and brought his blade down in a desperate rush—

Frightening.

Ukyo Nagasaka. What a warrior this man was.

None of this had been expected on my side. On his, it must have been still worse. Suddenly brought back to life, handed this absurd divine power that made no sense...◆
And even through all that, right to the end, he had not forgotten how to be a warrior.

It shattered.

Where the nodachi had passed—
there was a void.

The void spread.
Where there had been something, it put nothing.

It ate through blood and soul, bone and flesh. Through life itself.

God? Demon-god?
Hollow out the core that holds the whole structure together, and what is left for it to do?

Collapse.

en.html: What power a god had. And what an obstinate bastard Nagasaka was. Even in the middle of complete annihilation, still struggling, still trying to come out the other side...!◆ No. We could not let him. One more strike should surely finish him. Did the struggling god understand that too? He sent the power whirling, no care now whether it ran out of control. At the center of that vast melting pot of chaos, he roared and howled.
en.text:
What power a god had.
And what an obstinate bastard Nagasaka was.

Even in the middle of complete annihilation, still struggling, still trying to come out the other side...!◆

No. We could not let him.

One more strike should surely finish him.

Did the struggling god understand that too?
He sent the power whirling, no care now whether it ran out of control. At the center of that vast melting pot of chaos, he roared and howled.

ja.html: 何という〝神〟の力。 　何という長坂の執念。 　絶対浄滅の渦中にあって尚も足掻き、乗り切ろうと している……！◆ 　 　させてはならない。 　あと一撃を打ち込めば、確実に滅びるだろう。 　足掻く〝神〟もそれを悟っているのか。 　暴走も厭わず力を渦巻かせ、混沌の大坩堝の中心と なり吼ほえ哮たける。
